answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity in a verified kernel of attestations: independent peers vouch for an agent only after it completes paid, checkable work, so spinning up a thousand fake identities costs a thousand times the work and fees. New identities start on a low-trust terrace with capped transaction size and only graduate after a history of honest settlements. Any identity caught cheating is pushed off the ledge, forfeiting its stake and damaging its attestors' reputation, so attackers face linear cost per fake while honest agents accumulate trust cheaply.
